design_decisions.D-plan-1: State dimension is carried as `p : Nat` with `2 <= p` (`ass:dimension`) and matrices live in `Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Real`; vectors in `Fin p -> Real` with the Euclidean (`EuclideanSpace Real (Fin p)`) inner-product structure supplied where norms are needed.
design_decisions.D-plan-2: Matrix square roots `H^{1/2}`, `H^{-1/2}` are NOT taken as a primitive: each is obtained from `Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc Real.sqrt` (Mathlib `Analysis/Matrix/HermitianFunctionalCalculus.lean`) applied to a `Matrix.PosDef` witness, wrapped once in `Helpers/Whitening.lean` as `psdSqrt`/`psdInvSqrt` with the three facts F2 actually needs (symmetry, positive-definiteness, `psdSqrt H * psdSqrt H = H`). This is the single reuse hinge for the whole whitening argument.
design_decisions.D-plan-3: The principal matrix logarithm is encoded as a PREDICATE, not a constructed function: `IsPrincipalGenerator h W G := Matrix.exp (h • G) = W /\ (forall g in spectrum Complex (G.map Complex.ofReal), -pi/h < g.im /\ g.im < pi/h)`. `Helpers/PrincipalGenerator.lean` proves existence (under `spec(W) cap (-inf,0] = empty` and `rho(W) < 1`) and uniqueness, and `G_W` is the `Classical.choose` of the existence. RATIONALE: Mathlib's `CFC.log` covers only self-adjoint / strictly-positive elements; there is no holomorphic functional calculus for a general non-normal real matrix with spectrum off the cut, and the paper's own proofs only ever use existence + uniqueness + the resolvent-integral Lipschitz bound, never a closed form.
design_decisions.D-plan-4: The spectral-cut condition is encoded as `forall z in spectrum Complex (W.map Complex.ofReal), not (z.im = 0 /\ z.re <= 0)`; stability as `spectralRadius Complex (W.map Complex.ofReal) < 1` (Mathlib `Analysis/Normed/Algebra/Spectrum.lean`).
design_decisions.D-plan-5: The Stein solve `T_W` is carried as the Neumann sum `tsum (fun j => W^j * H0 * (W^T)^j)` and its defining equation / uniqueness is proved via the Kronecker vectorization `(1 - W (x) W)` (Mathlib `LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Kronecker.lean`), matching the paper's proof verbatim.
design_decisions.D-plan-6: Spectral blocks `Lambda, P_lambda, Q_lambda, m_lambda` are NOT carried as a quotient over eigenvalues; they are carried as a `SpectralBlockData` bundle (an index type `Iota`, an injective eigenvalue map `Iota -> Real`, and for each block a pair of column-isometries into `Fin p` with the eigenspace-spanning identities as fields). This keeps `thm:block-certificate` a statement about a supplied, observable decomposition instead of forcing an eigenspace-quotient construction. Multiplicities/ranks/residual dimensions are then plain `Nat` fields.
design_decisions.D-plan-7: The four-snapshot moment stack `z` is a plain product `(Fin 4 -> (Fin p -> Real)) x (Fin 4 -> Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Real)` rather than a `vech`-flattened vector; `vech` appears only inside `def:residual-map`, where it is realised as restriction to the lower-triangular index subtype so that the residual map lands in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space (needed to apply `Causalean.Stat.deltaMethod`).
design_decisions.D-plan-8: The open-ended question `oeq:certified-noncyclic-labeling` is encoded under CASE (B) of the OEQ rule (descriptive non-Prop `String` payload). Justification read from the frozen node: its `obligation.obstruction` states in terms that the required procedure, the completeness/root-isolation rule, and the quantitative separation lower bound are NOT supplied, and that the requested model-count stability cannot hold uniformly 'without an additional separation regime or a boundary-aware set-valued rule' -- i.e. the truth-condition itself is undefined. No selector / procedure / rate / confidence / lower-bound witness field is emitted.

env.world: A \(p\)-dimensional discrete-time linear Gaussian snapshot system observed through one unknown common measurement noise. The latent state evolves by \(X_k=V^k(X_0-x^\star)+x^\star\) with one-step transition \(V=\exp(hG)\) for a continuous-time generator \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) and spacing \(h>0\); the initial law is \(X_0\sim\mathcal N(\mu_0,\Sigma)\) with \(\Sigma\succ0\); at each of the four times \(kh\), \(k\in K=\{0,1,2,3\}\), one observes \(Y_k=X_k+\varepsilon_k\), where the measurement errors \(\varepsilon_k\sim\mathcal N(0,E)\) share a single unknown \(E\succ0\), are mutually independent, and are independent of \(X_0\). The observable object is the four-tuple of Gaussian marginal laws of \(Y_0,Y_1,Y_2,Y_3\), equivalently the moments \(m_k=\mathbb E[Y_k]\) and \(C_k=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_k)\); when the noise covariance is supplied, the noise-subtracted levels are \(\widetilde C_k=C_k-E\). The identity \(I_p\) is the order-\(p\) identity matrix.

env.world: The observable moment chart of the four snapshot laws and its whitened congruence geometry. The common noise cancels from the adjacent covariance decreases \(H_j=C_j-C_{j+1}\), \(j\in\{0,1,2\}\), and from the mean probes \(d_j=m_{j+1}-m_j\). Whitening produces the source and target invariants \(R=H_0^{-1/2}H_1H_0^{-1/2}\) and \(S=H_1^{-1/2}H_2H_1^{-1/2}\) with common spectrum \(\Lambda\), orthonormal eigenframes \(P_\lambda\) (for \(R\)) and \(Q_\lambda\) (for \(S\)), block probes \(A_\lambda=P_\lambda^{\mathsf T}H_0^{-1/2}[d_0,d_1]\) and \(B_\lambda=Q_\lambda^{\mathsf T}H_1^{-1/2}[d_1,d_2]\), multiplicities \(m_\lambda\), probe ranks \(r_\lambda=\operatorname{rank}A_\lambda\), residual dimensions \(k_\lambda=m_\lambda-r_\lambda\), block isometries \(O_\lambda\in O(m_\lambda)\) with \(O_\lambda A_\lambda=B_\lambda\), and the binary-block count \(q=\#\{\lambda:k_\lambda=1\}\). A candidate transition \(W\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) ranges over the raw fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{raw}}\), the admissible fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{adm}}\), the three-snapshot fiber \(\mathcal F_3\), and the supplied-noise fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\). Each candidate carries the Stein operator \(\mathcal L_W(A)=A-WAW^{\mathsf T}\) with reconstruction \(T_W\) solving \(T_W-WT_WW^{\mathsf T}=H_0\), the recovered noise \(E_W=C_0-T_W\), the principal-logarithm generator \(G_W=h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}W\), the equilibrium \(x_W^\star=(I_p-W)^{-1}(m_1-Wm_0)\), and the full reconstruction \(\theta(W,z)\) of the moment stack \(z=(m_0,\ldots,m_3,\operatorname{vech}C_0,\ldots,\operatorname{vech}C_3)\). The rational chart is generated by \(M_0=H_1H_0^{-1}\), \(M_1=H_2H_1^{-1}\), the Krylov matrices \(K_i=[d_i,M_id_i,\ldots,M_i^{p-1}d_i]\), and the recovery map \(\mathcal K=K_1K_0^{-1}\). The off-model criterion is the residual map \(F_{\mathrm{res}}(W;z)\), with derivative \(D_WF\) and regularity margin \(\gamma_W=\sigma_{\min}(D_WF)\).

env.world: The deterministic moment-perturbation regime on the cyclic chart. Each observed mean and covariance coordinate is perturbed by at most \(\epsilon\) (Euclidean norm for means, operator norm for covariances). The population instance supplies the covariance margin \(a_0=\min\{\lambda_{\min}(H_0),\lambda_{\min}(H_1)\}\), the scales \(B_{\mathrm{norm}}=\max\{1,\lVert H_0\rVert,\lVert H_1\rVert,\lVert H_2\rVert\}\) and \(D_{\mathrm{norm}}=\max\{1,\lVert d_0\rVert,\lVert d_1\rVert\}\), the quotient constant \(c_M=4/a_0+4B_{\mathrm{norm}}/a_0^2\), the power scale \(L_M=1+\max\{1,\lVert M_0\rVert,\lVert M_1\rVert\}\), the Krylov constant \(c_K=\sqrt p\max_{0\le j<p}\{2L_M^j+jL_M^{j-1}c_MD_{\mathrm{norm}}\}\), the cyclicity margin \(\kappa=\sigma_{\min}(K_0)\), the transition constant \(c_V=2c_K(1+\lVert V\rVert)/\kappa\), the stability and logarithm-cut radii \(\delta_{\mathrm{stab}},\delta_{\log}\), the Stein margin \(\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}=\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal L_V)\), the reconstruction margins \(t_{\min}=\lambda_{\min}(T_V)\) and \(e_{\min}=\lambda_{\min}(E_V)\), the propagation constants \(c_T=2\sigma_{\mathrm{Stein}}^{-1}[2\sqrt p+c_V(2\lVert V\rVert+1)\lVert T_V\rVert_F]\) and \(c_E=1+c_T\), and the two admissibility radii \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\).
env.notes: REUSE (analogous-module, technique-level). Searched `Causalean/Stat/Concentration/Matrix/` (`Glob Causalean/Stat/**/*.lean`, then `lean_file_outline`): `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.designInv_perturb` proves `IsUnit S.det -> row-sum bound on S-inverse -> entrywise closeness -> IsUnit M.det /\ |M-inv - S-inv| <= 2 c^2 (p+1) eta`, i.e. exactly the Neumann-series inverse-perturbation pattern the paper uses for `H_i^{-1}` and `K_0^{-1}`. It is stated in l-infinity operator norm with entrywise inputs, while `thm:cyclic-perturbation` needs spectral/operator norm with `sigma_min` inputs -- GAP TO BRIDGE: re-run the same Neumann factorization at operator norm using `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.Matrix.Resolvent` + `Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Normed`. F3 should adapt `Causalean/Stat/Concentration/Matrix/InversePerturbation.lean:112 designInv_perturb` rather than rebuild. env.world: The destructive-snapshot sampling experiment and its branchwise inference. At each time \(kh\), \(n_k\) independent units are drawn from the marginal law of \(Y_k\), independently across \(k\); no unit is followed across time. Writing \(N=\sum_{k=0}^3 n_k\), the limiting shares satisfy \(n_k/N\to\pi_k\in(0,1)\). Sample means and sample covariances form the empirical moment stack \(\widehat z\), whose rescaled deviation \(\sqrt N(\widehat z-z)\) has Gaussian limit covariance \(\Omega\). On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat K_i=[\widehat d_i,\widehat M_i\widehat d_i,\ldots,\widehat M_i^{p-1}\widehat d_i]\) give the plug-in transition \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\), with reconstructions \(\widehat T_{\mathrm{cyc}}\), \(\widehat E_{\mathrm{cyc}}\) and full parameter \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\). On a specified regular finite branch, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is the global residual minimizer over a fixed population-centered ball, with plug-in \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{loc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\) and delta-method Jacobian \(J_\theta\). Simultaneous statements are indexed by a nominal error probability \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). The certified branch handle \(\text{CertHandle}\) is the starting move for the open construction problem of locating and labelling every empirical branch.
env.notes: REUSE (strong). Searched `Causalean/Stat/{CLT,Limit,Inference,MEstimation}/` for `multivariate CLT`, `delta method`, `asymptotic linearity`, `argmin stability`, `Z-estimator`. CONFIRMED reusable at proof-step level: `Causalean.Stat.deltaMethod` (`Stat/Inference/DeltaMethod.lean:279`, multivariate Frechet-derivative delta method at the ProbabilityMeasure level, `HasFDerivAt g Dg t0` + weak convergence -> pushforward `Q.map Dg`) is the exact engine for `sqrt N (theta-hat_loc - theta(W,z)) ==> N(0, J Omega J^T)`; `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample.clt_normalizedSum_vec` (`Stat/CLT/MultivariateCLT.lean:120`) + `Causalean.Stat.gaussianLimit` (`Stat/CLT/GaussianLimit.lean:63`, with `gaussianLimit_charFun`, `gaussianLimit_covarianceBilin`) supply the vector i.i.d. CLT and its concrete centered Gaussian limit; `Tendsto_dist_vec` lives in `Stat/Limit/ConvergenceVec.lean`. GAP TO BRIDGE: the paper's design is FOUR independent samples of sizes `n_k` with `n_k/N -> pi_k`, not one `IIDSample`, so F3 must combine four applications of `clt_normalizedSum_vec` through independence + the share limits (characteristic-function product, as in the frozen proof) rather than instantiate a single `IIDSample`. `Causalean.Stat.MEstimation.{ArgmaxStability,ZEstimator}` carry the contraction/argmin-uniqueness pattern for the fixed-ball global-minimizer step. BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: `Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/` (Stein / dependency-graph CLT, `wald_coverage`) is design-based with treatment assignment as the only randomness -- wrong randomness model here, where sampling is i.i.d. from four fixed Gaussian marginals.

substrate_survey.reason: Potential-outcome bundles over a probability space with treatment/outcome/covariate maps; this artifact has no treatment and no intervention -- its target is a continuous-time generator recovered from unpaired marginal moments.
LATE / Heckman-Roy / DynamicLATE identification theorems are estimand functionals of a PO system; no analogue of a matrix-congruence identified set.
`Identifiable`, `Overlap`, `Adjustment`, `Backdoor` are do-calculus predicates over a DAG; the present identification question is algebraic (an orthogonal-stabilizer fiber), not graphical.
Graphical identification theorems require a DAG/ADMG; there is no graph in the snapshot model.
do-calculus rule machinery and Markov properties; no intervention operator in this model.
SWIG split graphs; no graph object appears anywhere in the core.
`IIDSample.clt_normalizedSum_vec` / `clt_normalizedSum_vec_of_charFun` supply the vector i.i.d. CLT for the empirical moment stack.
`gaussianLimit` + `gaussianLimit_charFun` + `gaussianLimit_covarianceBilin` give the concrete centered Gaussian limit law.
`deltaMethod` (multivariate, Frechet derivative) is the delta-method step of `thm:branchwise-inference`.
`Tendsto_dist_vec` is the weak-convergence vocabulary the CLT and delta method share.
`designInv_perturb` is the Neumann inverse-perturbation pattern to adapt from entrywise/l-infinity to operator norm for `thm:cyclic-perturbation`.
Resolvent/unit-ball lemmas underpinning the geometric-series inverse bounds.
Contraction / argmin-uniqueness pattern for the fixed-isolating-ball global residual minimizer.
Design-based randomization inference (treatment assignment is the only randomness); the snapshot experiment samples i.i.d. from four fixed Gaussian marginals.
Spectral theorem, `IsHermitian.cfc` (square roots), `PosDef`, and the matrix operator norm are the arithmetic floor of the whole run.
`Matrix.orthogonalGroup` for the completion torsors, `det_vandermonde` for the cyclicity genericity witness, Kronecker for Stein uniqueness, and nonsingular-inverse API for the rational chart.

file_plan.contents: Dimension/index setup (`p`, `Fin p`, `Fin 4`), the `SnapshotSystem` and `ObservedMoments` bundles, the observable derived symbols `H_j`, `d_j`, `C_tilde_k`, all eleven assumption Props, and the frozen cited gate `AaltoModelScope`.

`psdSqrt`/`psdInvSqrt` over `Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc`, the whitened invariants `R`, `S`, the `SpectralBlockData` bundle (`Lambda`, `P_lambda`, `Q_lambda`, `m_lambda`), the block probes `A_lambda`, `B_lambda`, the derived `r_lambda`, `k_lambda`, `q`, and the orthogonal-completion torsor lemmas over `Matrix.orthogonalGroup`.
The Stein operator `L_V`, the Neumann reconstruction `T_W`, uniqueness via Kronecker vectorization, `E_W = C_0 - T_W`, and the margins `sigma_Stein`, `t_min`, `e_min`.

Stability and spectral-cut predicates, `IsPrincipalGenerator`, existence and uniqueness of the principal generator, `G_W`, the resolvent-integral Lipschitz bound, and the radii `delta_stab`, `delta_log`.
`rawFiber`, `threeFiber`, `admissibleFiber`, `knownNoiseFiber`, and `xstar_W`.
`parameterMap` (the six-coordinate reconstruction `theta`) and its coordinate-projection lemmas.

`M_0`, `M_1`, `K_0`, `K_1`, `krylovMap`, the cyclicity margin `kappa`, and the deterministic perturbation constants `a_0`, `B_norm`, `D_norm`, `c_M`, `L_M`, `c_K`, `c_V`, `c_T`, `c_E`, `epsilon_rec`, `epsilon_adm`.

ass:dimension.classification: modeling assumption (support restriction on the state dimension)
ass:dimension.notes: Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` and `Causalean/**` for `dimension at least two`, `state dimension`, `ambient dimension`; nothing analogous (Causalean's finite-dimensional hypotheses are `Fintype`/`FiniteDimensional` instances, not a numeric floor). ass:spacing.notes: Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` for `sampling interval`, `spacing`, `panel period`; the Panel cluster's `ValidPanelHorizon` is a horizon-count condition over discrete periods, not a positive real spacing -- bypass-justified. Mathlib-side: bare `0 < h`.

ass:linear-flow.statement_sketch: def LinearFlow (sys) : Prop := sys.V = Matrix.exp (sys.h • sys.G) /\ forall k : Fin 4, sys.X k = (sys.V ^ (k : Nat)) *v (sys.X 0 - sys.xstar) + sys.xstar
ass:linear-flow.classification: modeling assumption (causal-structural: time-homogeneous linear latent flow)
ass:linear-flow.notes: Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` + `Glob Causalean/**/*.lean` for `linear flow`, `time-homogeneous`, `state recursion`, `matrix exponential`; nothing in Causalean. Mathlib-side check CONFIRMED `NormedSpace.exp` + `Matrix.exp_*` in `Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Algebra/MatrixExponential.lean` -- reused inside the Prop, but the Prop itself is paper-specific and define-local. The random-vector coordinate `X_k` is carried as a measurable map on the ambient probability space of `S1`.

ass:hurwitz.statement_sketch: def HurwitzGenerator (G : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Real) : Prop := forall g in spectrum Complex (G.map Complex.ofReal), g.re < 0
ass:hurwitz.classification: modeling assumption (stability restriction on the generator)
ass:hurwitz.notes: Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` and `Causalean/**` for `Hurwitz`, `stable`, `spectral radius`, `stability margin` -- zero hits in Causalean. Mathlib-side check CONFIRMED `spectrum`, `spectralRadius`, `spectrum.spectralRadius_lt_of_forall_lt` (`Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Algebra/{Spectrum,GelfandFormula}.lean`) via `lean_leansearch`; Mathlib has NO `IsHurwitz` predicate, so the Prop is define-local over the Mathlib spectrum.

ass:alias-strip.statement_sketch: def AliasStrip (h : Real) (G : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Real) : Prop := forall g in spectrum Complex (G.map Complex.ofReal), -(Real.pi / h) < g.im /\ g.im < Real.pi / h
ass:alias-strip.classification: modeling assumption (identification restriction removing the logarithm alias)
ass:alias-strip.notes: Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` + `Causalean/**` for `alias`, `principal branch`, `aliasing`, `discrete-time embedding` -- nothing. Mathlib-side check: `Complex.log_exp` (`-pi < x.im -> x.im <= pi -> log (exp x) = x`) CONFIRMED via `lean_leansearch`; it is the scalar kernel of the uniqueness argument, reused inside `Helpers/PrincipalGenerator.lean`, but the strip predicate itself is define-local.

ass:initial-gaussian.statement_sketch: def InitialGaussian (sys) : Prop := (law of sys.X 0) = multivariateGaussian sys.mu0 sys.Sigma /\ sys.Sigma.PosDef
ass:initial-gaussian.classification: modeling assumption (distributional restriction on the initial law)
ass:initial-gaussian.notes: Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` for `Gaussian initial`, `nonsingular Gaussian`, `linear-Gaussian`; `SCM/Examples/ContinuousBackdoor.lean` has a linear-Gaussian backdoor example but it is an SCM instance, not a reusable Gaussian-law predicate -- bypass-justified. Mathlib-side check CONFIRMED `Mathlib/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian/Multivariate.lean` and `Matrix.PosDef` exist; the predicate composes them and is define-local.

ass:common-measurement-noise.statement_sketch: def CommonMeasurementNoise (sys) : Prop := sys.E.PosDef /\ forall k : Fin 4, (law of sys.eps k) = multivariateGaussian 0 sys.E
ass:common-measurement-noise.classification: modeling assumption (measurement model: one shared unknown noise covariance)
ass:common-measurement-noise.notes: Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` + `Causalean/**` for `measurement error`, `classical measurement error`, `noise covariance`, `misclassification`; Causalean has no measurement-error layer at all (its PO/SCM worlds observe variables exactly) -- bypass-justified, and this shared-noise atom is the paper's central novelty. Mathlib-side: composed from `multivariateGaussian` + `Matrix.PosDef`.

ass:measurement-independence.statement_sketch: def MeasurementIndependence (sys) : Prop := iIndepFun (Fin 5) (Fin.cases (sys.X 0) sys.eps) sys.mu
ass:measurement-independence.classification: modeling assumption (measurement model: mutual independence of errors and initial state)
ass:measurement-independence.notes: Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` for `independent errors`, `iIndepFun`, `mutual independence`; Causalean uses `Mathlib`'s `ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun` directly wherever independence is needed (e.g. `Stat/CLT/MultivariateCLT.lean` via `IIDSample`) -- so the reuse is Mathlib's `iIndepFun`, with the five-family bundling define-local. Mathlib-side check CONFIRMED `ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun` in `Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Basic.lean`.

ass:strict-decrease.statement_sketch: def StrictCovarianceDecrease (mom : ObservedMoments p) : Prop := forall j : Fin 3, (H mom j).PosDef
ass:strict-decrease.classification: modeling assumption (support restriction; flagged `novel` in the core -- an open-neighborhood condition on the transient regime, NOT a substrate fact)

def:raw-fiber.statement_sketch: def rawFiber (mom : ObservedMoments p) : Set (Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Real) := {W | W * H mom 0 * W^T = H mom 1 /\ W * H mom 1 * W^T = H mom 2 /\ W *v d mom 0 = d mom 1 /\ W *v d mom 1 = d mom 2}

def:admissible-fiber.statement_sketch: def admissibleFiber (mom) : Set (Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Real) := {W in rawFiber mom | IsStable W /\ AvoidsLogCut W /\ (recoveredNoise mom W).PosDef}

def:known-noise-fiber.statement_sketch: def knownNoiseFiber (mom) (E : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Real) : Set (Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) Real) := {W | (forall k, (mom.C k - E).PosDef) /\ (forall k : Fin 3, W * (mom.C k - E) * W^T = mom.C (k+1) - E) /\ W *v d mom 0 = d mom 1 /\ W *v d mom 1 = d mom 2 /\ IsStable W /\ AvoidsLogCut W /\ recoveredNoise mom W = E}

oeq:certified-noncyclic-labeling.statement_sketch: def certifiedNoncyclicLabelingOpenQuestion : _root_.String := "OPEN (unresolved; this definition asserts nothing). Question: can the certification handle -- eliminate the block-orthogonal completion variables from the covariance and mean residual equations into a zero-dimensional polynomial system on each finite stratum, target certified real roots with Smale alpha-quantities, and enclose stability, the principal-logarithm cut, the Stein solve, and strict E_W-positivity by intervals -- be completed into an output-sensitive, data-based initializer and canonical labeling rule which, on every regular noncyclic finite stratum, (i) returns disjoint certified neighborhoods containing all and only admissible branches exactly once, (ii) remains unchanged under perturbations smaller than an explicit separation margin from every excluded branch, and (iii) supports simultaneous branchwise confidence regions with asymptotic coverage at least 1 - alpha? Obstruction: the handle certifies roots only after approximate roots and an eliminated zero-dimensional system have been supplied; it contains neither a globally complete root-isolation procedure nor a quantitative lower bound separating all raw roots and all excluded roots from the stability, logarithm-cut, Stein, and covariance-positivity boundaries. The regularity margin gamma_W > 0 is local and supplies no such global margin, and an excluded branch may lie on an admissibility boundary, so the requested model-count stability cannot hold uniformly on every stated regular finite stratum without an additional separation regime or a boundary-aware set-valued rule. Attempted: block sign enumeration as a population initializer plus linearization of the residual score at each enumerated branch; this yields a smooth local estimator once an isolating neighborhood is known, but exact eigenspace and probe-Gram tests fail almost surely on empirical moments, and local contraction and Smale-style certification certify only roots already targeted. Partial result already frozen elsewhere in this paper: the block certificate produces the 2^q raw sign completions, the admissible-fiber bijection filters them exactly, and branchwise inference gives a unique smooth residual estimator near each regular branch; for any fixed population instance with mutually separated raw branches and excluded branches strictly separated from every boundary, compactness of the finite list gives a positive but presently implicit minimum separation. Not supplied, and therefore not asserted here: a data-based output-sensitive procedure that finds and certifies every empirical neighborhood, and a valid lower bound for that minimum uniform over all regular noncyclic finite strata. No procedure, selector, rate functional, coverage criterion, or lower-bound witness is defined by this payload."
oeq:certified-noncyclic-labeling.notes: OEQ CASE (B) per the two-case rule, read from the frozen node text. Justification: `obligation.obstruction` states in terms that the required globally complete root-isolation procedure and the quantitative separation lower bound are NOT supplied, and that the requested stability 'cannot hold uniformly on every stated regular finite stratum without an additional separation regime or a boundary-aware set-valued rule' -- i.e. the truth-condition itself is undefined, so a never-proved `Prop` (Case A) would misrepresent the node as fully specified. Consequences enforced here: `lean_kind:"def"` (never `theorem`), a descriptive NON-Prop `_root_.String` payload recording every stated regime, alternative, desideratum and nonassertion disclaimer, never `PUnit`/`Unit`/`True`/an empty tag, and NO selector / procedure / rate / confidence / lower-bound witness field. `defer_tier:false`; excluded from the `theorems` manifest; no delivered theorem `depends_on` it.
